summary: To ship OAuth for LinkedIn, the developer must create a LinkedIn Developer application, configure an HTTPS redirect URI under the Auth tab, request necessary member authorization scopes, and implement the 3-legged OAuth code flow to exchange authorization codes for access tokens.
difficulty_reason: Basic developer applications can be set up self-serve in minutes, though certain specific partner products or higher tiers may require additional review or gating.

evidence.quote: A LinkedIn Developer application to create a new application or select your existing application

requirements.text: Prior authorization access granted for at least one 3-legged OAuth permission

evidence.quote: Prior authorization access granted for at least one 3-legged OAuth permission.

steps.text: Go to the LinkedIn Developer Portal and create a new application or select your existing application.

evidence.quote: Select your application in the LinkedIn Developer Portal.

steps.title: Create or Select a LinkedIn Developer Application

steps.text: Navigate to the Auth tab of your application in the LinkedIn Developer Portal and add your absolute HTTPS redirect (callback) URL under Authorized redirect URLs, then save changes.

evidence.quote: Click the Auth tab to view your application credentials. Add the redirect (callback) URL via HTTPS to your server.
Under Authorized redirect URLs, add your redirect URI Save changes

steps.title: Configure Redirect URLs

steps.text: Direct the user's browser to LinkedIn's OAuth 2.0 authorization page with your response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, state, and a space-delimited, URL-encoded scope parameter.
steps.title: Request an Authorization Code

steps.text: Make an HTTP POST request to the accessToken endpoint with grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret, and redirect_uri using a Content-Type of x-www-form-urlencoded.
steps.title: Exchange Authorization Code for an Access Token

steps.text: Include the Bearer access token in the Authorization header to make API requests on behalf of the member.

evidence.quote: Once you've obtained an access token, you can start making authenticated API requests on behalf of the member by including an Authorization header

steps.title: Make Authenticated API Requests

nuances.text: The redirect URI must be absolute, use HTTPS, cannot include a hash fragment, and must match registered URLs exactly (wildcard/prefix matching is not supported, and only the state parameter may vary at runtime).

evidence.quote: Wildcard or prefix matching is not supported. The only exception is the OAuth 2.0 state parameter, which may vary per request and is ignored during validation.

nuances.text: Access tokens are issued with a 60-day lifespan (5184000 seconds).

evidence.quote: Currently, all access tokens are issued with a 60-day lifespan.

nuances.text: Authorization codes have a 30-minute lifespan and must be used immediately.

evidence.quote: For security reasons, the authorization code has a 30-minute lifespan and must be used immediately.

nuances.text: If you request a different scope than the previously granted scope, all previous access tokens are invalidated.

evidence.quote: If you request a different scope than the previously granted scope, all the previous access tokens are invalidated.

blockers.issue: Redirect fails or member stays stuck on LinkedIn after verification
blockers.why_it_happens: The provided redirectUri does not exactly match a registered URL, is missing, empty, improperly encoded, or includes unsupported extra query parameters.
blockers.workaround: Ensure the redirectUri is an exact match to a registered URL and is properly URL-encoded.

evidence.quote: Automatic redirection back to your application will not occur in the following scenarios: The provided redirectUri does not exactly match a URL registered in the LinkedIn Developer Portal

agent_can_do: Exchange authorization code for access token via API POST
Make authenticated API requests using the access token
developer_must_do: Configure authorized redirect URLs in the LinkedIn Developer Portal
